ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the PRC; Foreign Investment Law (2019); Regulations on the Administration of Road Transportation; Customs and TIR implementing regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Commercial and Industrial Service Portal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization-equivalent under the Cross-Strait mechanism: Taiwan district court notarization, then Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification, then Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) verification on the mainland. Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille member and no PRC consulate exists in Taiwan, so Hague Apostille is not available and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Company Registration and/or Tax Clearance Certificate) of Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs; Taiwan National Taxation Administration under the Ministry of Finance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization-equivalent under the Cross-Strait mechanism: Taiwan district court notarization, then SEF verification, then ARATS verification. This path supersedes Hague Apostille and ordinary consular legalization for Taiwan-origin documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing WFOE incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of Taiwan investing company, notarized before a Taiwan district court notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization-equivalent under the Cross-Strait mechanism: Taiwan notarial certification, SEF verification, ARATS verification; the executed POA must expressly authorize mainland counsel and local representatives to sign incorporation filings.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investing company and the corporate records maintained by Taiwan MOEA
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization-equivalent under the Cross-Strait mechanism: Taiwan district court notarization of authenticated copy, SEF verification, ARATS verification; no apostille because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention Contracting Party.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from Taiwan bank evidencing financial standing and transaction history
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Settlement bank of Taiwan investing company in Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization-equivalent under the Cross-Strait mechanism: notarized confirmation of bank officer signatory authority, SEF verification, ARATS verification; bank letter must be issued within 90 days and remain current for AML/UBO and capital payment verification.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to any filing, run mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, directors, officers, and senior operational managers against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU restrictive measures, PRC sanctioned entity and individual lists, and Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission PEP databases. Screening must also identify politically exposed persons including Taiwan central and local elected officials, judges, military officers, state-owned enterprise executives, and their immediate family members and close associates. Any PEP or sanction hit requires enhanced due diligence, written source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior compliance officer approval, and escalation for cross-border trucking/TIR license review. Positive hits may not be auto-cleared; all clearance decisions must be documented and retained for five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration and Reservation System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in simplified Chinese and follow the four-tier statutory structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or business characteristic + organizational form. The WFOE limited liability name must end in 有限公司 (rendered as 'Co., Ltd.' in English filings). Traditional Chinese may not be used in the official registry; Taiwanese investor names and corporate names must be transliterated or converted into simplified Chinese in accordance with the official cross-strait document verification standards. An auxiliary English name may be filed for customs, TIR carnets, and foreign exchange purposes, but it cannot replace the Chinese legal name and must be consistent with the Chinese name in meaning where required by SAMR.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant should first obtain or download the written rejection notice stating the statutory basis. Within 15 days of rejection, the applicant may submit supplementary materials or an alternative name to the registration authority. If the authority still refuses, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the SAMR at the next higher level within 60 days of receiving the written rejection, attaching the name screening results, evidence of no confusing similarity, and, where applicable, ministerial approvals for sensitive tokens. If administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within 15 days after service of the reconsideration decision. For cross-strait structures, the Taiwan investor's POA holder should be expressly authorized to make name reservation amendments and appeals without repeated notarization.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address will be rejected as the registered address of the WFOE in the road-freight and TIR logistics industry. The Company Law and PRC registration regulations require a permanent physical business premises within the registered administrative district. The road transportation license requires actual offices, operational communications, parking and vehicle dispatch facilities, customs and bonded transport records, and tax/accounting books at the local address. Municipal tax authorities and customs will not accept a virtual mailbox for a WFOE operating long-haul bonded trucking, especially because SWIFT wire and fuel card clearing require stable corporate financial records and physical invoice issuance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (approximately 70% probability of unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months after incorporation). Checklist for expected municipal tax, market supervision, and transport authority inspections: (1) physical address signboard matching the registered name; (2) lease contract, property ownership certificate, or land-use certificate; (3) presence of manager or responsible person at the registered premises during business hours; (4) corporate seal, invoices, road transport permits, TIR carnet custody controls, and customs bonded records; (5) fuel card contracts and banking records aligned with the registered business scope; (6) proof of actual parking or logistics coordination capability in the stated city.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Articles 128-156, 202, 208, and 387; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 7-8; Act Governing Relations between Peoples of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area; Regulations Governing Investment Permission in Taiwan by Mainland Investors.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; Investment Commission, MOEA for mainland-source investment permission.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration under Article 387 of the Taiwan Company Act, together with the executed Articles of Incorporation and capital verification certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed by Taiwan Company Act for a limited liability company. However, for the ISIC 5221 cross-border TIR trucking licence, the Ministry of Transportation and Communications requires paid-in capital of at least NT$5,000,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash at par, verified by a certified public accountant. The capital is deposited in the company's Taiwan bank account and is not escrow-blocked; it may be deployed only after registration and the transport licence are obtained, and it cannot be withdrawn below the regulator's solvency requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, on this ___ day of ________, 20___, the first meeting of the Board of Directors of CN__TW__CN_WFOE_LTD was held at the registered office in Taiwan. Notice being duly given and all directors being present, a quorum was confirmed. The Board unanimously adopted the following resolutions. 1. Share Capital Subscription and Issue: the subscription statement presented to the Board, under which the promoters and the sole shareholder subscribed for ordinary shares at par, is accepted; the aggregate paid-in capital of NT$5,000,000 is ratified; the Company is authorised to issue share certificates; the register of shareholders and corporate seal shall be kept at the registered office; and a certified public accountant shall verify that the capital is received in cash in the Company's Taiwan bank account before any operating licence is obtained. 2. Banking Authorization: the Chairman, General Manager and Chief Financial Officer, acting in any two-person combination, are authorised to open domestic, foreign-currency, customs-bond, payroll and fuel-card clearing accounts with licensed banks, and to execute bank mandates, electronic banking agreements, wire transfer instructions and letters of credit; any payment exceeding NT$500,000 requires two authorised signatures. 3. Registered Office: the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation; the Company nameplate shall be installed; all statutory registers, minutes, share-records and the common seal shall be maintained at that address; and the Company Secretary shall notify the Department of Commerce of that address. 4. Statutory Officers and Authorised Signatories: [Name A] is appointed Chairman and General Manager, [Name B] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, [Name C] is appointed Company Secretary, and [Name D] is appointed TIR Customs Compliance Officer, each to hold office until the next annual meeting; the General Manager and Company Secretary, jointly, are authorised to sign and file formation instruments, corporate resolutions, tax registrations, transport and TIR licence applications, environmental registrations, fire-safety declarations, and all banking and customs documents; and the Company Secretary may certify copies and appear before government authorities. These resolutions are immediately effective and shall be entered in the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Mainland Investor Investment Permission from the Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan / Invest Taiwan online application portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form A for investment-by-application using the Invest Taiwan portal after signing the parent-company investment resolution and an engagement letter for the local formation agent. Disclose the ultimate beneficial owner, proposed capital amount, line of business as ISIC 5221 cross-border TIR trucking, and the legal form of the Taiwan entity. Attach notarized corporate existence documents of the mainland Chinese parent, audited financial statements, the proposed business plan, and a lawful source-of-funds declaration. If the Commission raises a security or sector concern, the applicant has one opportunity to amend the business plan. After the Commission issues the investment approval letter, the company may open bank accounts and submit company registration. No operational activity is permitted before the approval letter.
required_dossiers: Form A investment application
Resolution of the mainland parent board approving the Taiwan investment
Certificate of incorporation and articles of the mainland parent, notarized and authenticated
Parent audited financial statements for the previous two years
Proposed Taiwan company business plan and projected financials
Investment trust agreement or power of attorney to local formation agent
Declaration of source-of-funds and AML-KYC information
Passport or ID copies of ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit missing translations or accounting evidence within 30 days. If the investment is rejected on public-interest grounds, file an administrative appeal with the Executive Yuan or prepare a revised structure that preserves foreign investment while limiting equity or sensitive business scope.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Accounts and File CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Taiwan and certified public accountant approved under Taiwan Company Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Investment Commission approval letter, apply for company name pre-reservation through the Department of Commerce online registry, then visit a licensed Taiwan bank to open a temporary capital deposit account in the name of the proposed company. The mainland parent must transfer the subscribed capital amount by wire from an external banking channel; the bank will issue a deposit certificate. Engage a Taiwan certified public accountant to review the bank certificate and subscription ledgers and issue a capital verification report. The CPA must confirm that the capital is freely available in cash and not a loan. The verified capital report will be attached to the company registration application. The temporary account is converted into the operating account after registration.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission approval letter
Name pre-reservation certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Passports/ARC of directors
Bank account application and AML-CIP forms
Share subscription statement
Bank deposit certificate confirming received funds
CPA capital verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account due to money-laundering concerns, submit the Investment Commission letter, source-of-wealth records, and a bilingual corporate chart. If the CPA refuses to certify, reconcile intercompany transfer labels and provide bank SWIFT confirmation, then resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles of Incorporation and File Company Registration with MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan / Company Registration Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After capital verification, prepare final Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, English name, business purpose (ISIC 5221 and TIR cross-border trucking), number of shares and par value, registered office address, number of directors, and appointment of managers. The shareholders and directors must sign the articles in counterparts; if any counterpart is signed outside Taiwan, it must be notarized and authenticated. Submit the Company Registration Application online with the investment approval letter, articles, director consent letters, office-use consent, capital verification report and bank certificate. The Department of Commerce will issue a Company Registration Certificate and a Unified Business Number. This certificate is the foundation for all subsequent operational permits.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application Form
Original counterpart of Articles of Incorporation
Director, supervisor and manager consent letters and identity documents
Registered office lease or consent of owner
CPA capital verification report and bank deposit certificate
Mainland investment approval letter
Foreign company / statutory representative power of attorney
Confirmation of company seal impression
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry sends a correction notice, revise within the stated 7-day window and upload a redlined version. If the name or business scope is rejected, file a new name application or amend business scope to exclude regulated goods; any final refusal can be appealed administratively under the Administrative Procedure Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Customs, Labour and Uniform-Invoice Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (regional branch of Ministry of Finance), Taiwan Customs Administration, Bureau of Labor Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Unified Business Number, register with the regional National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise income tax and business tax. Apply for acquisition of tax control equipment or registered e-invoice service so the company can issue uniform invoices. If the company will undertake TIR bonded trucking, register as a TIR authorized consignor with Taiwan Customs and apply for any necessary customs security or TIR guarantee. Register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance for labor insurance, health insurance and pension; open a payroll bank account and designate a tax withholding agent. This registration is separate from the transport licence and must be completed before fundraising or import/export statements.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate and Unified Business Number
Articles of Incorporation
Tax registration application form and seal impression
Bank account proof
Lease agreement for the office/garage
Customs registration application
TIR Carnet holder application or guarantee agreement
Labor and health insurance employer registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is suspended for inconsistency in registered business scope, amend the Articles first and re-file. For customs delays, obtain a provisional customs code by submitting a written undertaking; if insurance registration late, pay back premiums and file an amnesty declaration with the Bureau.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Cross-Border Trucking Licence and TIR Operational Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC), Directorate General of Highways / regional Motor Vehicle Offices; Taiwan Customs Administration for TIR Carnet authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal freight-carrier application to the MOTC district motor vehicle office, proving that the company has sufficient paid-in capital, fleet vehicles (owned or under long-term lease), a secure terminal or parking lot, and qualified professional drivers holding the TIR certificate. Include the Company Registration Certificate, financial statements, capital verification certificate, vehicle list and inspection reports, garage site certificates, and insurance cover. After receiving the road freight transport business licence, apply to Taiwan Customs for recognized TIR Carnet holder status, submitting the MOTC licence, a TIR guarantee contract (through the national guarantee association or IRU chain), and a customs operating plan for sealed bonded vehicles. Customs may inspect the registered office and depot. Only after all clearances may the company haul bonded cargo under TIR Carnets.
required_dossiers: Freight-carrier license application form
MOTC minimum capital proof
Vehicle registration certificates or leases and inspection reports
Registered address and parking/depot consent
TIR driver professional qualification certificates
Road freight liability insurance certificates
TIR Carnet holder application and guarantee contract
Annual financial statements and cash-flow projection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOTC rejects the fleet size, provide purchase orders or ratified leases for additional vehicles and refile after the fleet is registered. If customs rejects TIR guarantee, increase the guarantee limit or file a single-journey TIR Carnet with a cash bond; any denial may be appealed administratively within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC), Directorate General of Highways; Department of Commerce, MOEA; municipal building and fire departments for site clearances.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cross-border freight transport business licence issued by MOTC, plus TIR Carnet holder authorization issued by Taiwan Customs Administration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Taiwan (Environmental Protection Administration)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable for office-only TIR administration; Environmental Registration (Category II self-declaration) required for vehicle maintenance depots, cargo consolidation warehouses, or fuel storage with diesel capacity above 3,000 liters; Full EIA Report required only for hazardous-goods terminals in sensitive zones or floor area over 15,000 m².
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For Category II depots, wastewater must meet pH 6-9, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, SS ≤ 30 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L before discharge. VOC emissions from painting/degreasing operations must not exceed 0.6 kg/hour; fugitive VOCs in the workplace must remain below Taiwan MOL permissible exposure limits. Hazardous waste such as used oil, spent filters, batteries, and oily rags must be stored in sealed containers in a bonded area and delivered to licensed hazardous-waste carriers within the statutory retention time under Taiwan Waste Disposal Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense fire-safety approval is required for the registered office, terminal garage, and any warehouse used for bonded cargo staging. The licensed fire authority must issue a Fire Safety Certification after inspection of extinguishers, hydrants, emergency lighting, signage, and evacuation routes. If vehicles are serviced on site, an Occupational Safety clearance under Taiwan Occupational Safety and Health Act is required for pits, lifts, ventilation, and hazardous material storage. Structural load inspection is required for any mezzanine or racking above 2 meters.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, administered locally by the provincial and municipal competent tax bureaux; online electronic portal: STA Electronic Tax Hall (e-Tax) plus provincial e-Tax modules; official gateway: chinatax.gov.cn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) under the integrated market-entity registration procedure, including the Foreign Investment Information Report for the foreign shareholder. Step 2: Through the multi-certificate one-stop integration, the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on the Business License is automatically registered with STA and becomes the taxpayer identification number (TIN). Step 3: Complete supplementary tax registration in the Electronic Tax Hall within 30 days of issuance: select VAT taxpayer status (general or small-scale), file legal representative real-name authentication, designate the competent tax bureau, register bank account and report expected taxable scope. Step 4: Activate the e-identification digital certificate (CA) for electronic declarations and e-invoice issuance. Step 5: For a foreign non-resident enterprise that has no permanent establishment or WFOE status, the person paying the China-source income must perform withholding registration; if the foreign investor nonetheless needs a direct Chinese TIN, apply to the competent tax bureau where the income arises for non-resident registration and treaty-based relief. The WFOE itself is a Chinese resident taxpayer and does not obtain a separate non-resident TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the WFOE limited liability company is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed on worldwide taxable income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law; no pass-through or transparent classification is permitted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification: no check-the-box elections and no hybrid mismatch election under Chinese tax law. The only meaningful election is VAT taxpayer status: an enterprise with annual taxable turnover below RMB 5,000,000 may elect general VAT taxpayer status to recover input VAT, while mandatory general registration applies above that threshold. Export zero-rating election is available if the statutory export evidence package is complete.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT Law and its implementing regulations; no separate GST. Freight transport services are subject to the 9% VAT band and international/export freight transport qualifies for the 0% zero-rating band.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover. Any WFOE making taxable supplies must complete VAT/tax registration upon establishment; below RMB 5,000,000 small-scale taxpayer status may apply, and above RMB 5,000,000 registration as a general VAT taxpayer is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a fiscally controlled e-invoicing environment administered by STA. General VAT taxpayers must issue Special Value-Added Tax Invoices or fully digitalized electronic invoices (FDEI) through the STA electronic invoice service platform or approved tax-control software. Invoice data must be transmitted to the STA's Golden Tax System III in real time or near-real time. Each invoice carries a unique tax-control serial number and anti-fraud verification code, commonly described as 'one invoice, one code', and can be verified on the national VAT invoice verification portal. For export zero-rating, the zero-rated e-invoice must cross-reference the customs export declaration number and the foreign exchange collection record.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods is zero-rated only if the goods are declared and physically leave the customs territory of mainland China, the WFOE is a general VAT taxpayer, a legitimate export sales contract exists, and the export proceeds are repatriated through banks. For international road freight transport under TIR Carnets, the cross-border transport service provided to a non-resident customer and commencing or ending outside mainland China is zero-rated as an international transport service; however, any domestic portion must be segregated or treated as part of the zero-rated international carriage only under a single cross-border contract supported by TIR and CMR documentation. The claim must be supported by customs exit records, TIR Carnet data and foreign-exchange collection evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (China Export Goods Declaration Form; export counterpart of a Bill of Entry) with TIR Carnet customs endorsement
TIR Carnet and matching TIR-EPD (TIR Electronic PreDeclaration) acceptance record
CMR international road consignment note or equivalent Bill of Lading/waybill evidencing cross-border movement
Export freight transport contract or invoice with the zero-rated VAT entry
Bank-issued Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or SAFE trade foreign-exchange collection and settlement verification record
Export VAT zero-rating declaration submitted through the STA Electronic Tax Hall
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and China Customs jointly audit export zero-rating claims. If the export declaration, TIR/CMR route evidence, commercial invoice, or foreign-exchange repatriation record is false or incomplete, the zero-rating is reversed and the services/goods are recharacterized as domestic taxable supplies. The taxpayer must then pay unremitted VAT at the applicable rate (for freight transport, 9%) plus any unremitted city maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax if tax evasion is found. Any VAT refund already paid is clawed back with interest. Fraudulent export-refund claims can be prosecuted under the PRC Criminal Law for export tax-refund fraud; the statutory recovery period is unlimited for fraud, and shifts to the general three-year (or five-year if the amount exceeds RMB 100,000) limitation for non-fraud administrative recovery.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains current account convertibility under the PBOC-SAFE framework, while capital account transactions remain subject to approval and registration controls. CNY is freely convertible for trade and service payments upon genuine transaction documentation, but not for full capital-account fungibility. A CN WFOE must open current-account foreign exchange accounts at designated banks, and every inbound equity remittance is treated as FDI and tracked in SAFE's capital account information system. Profit repatriation by the Taiwan shareholder is permitted after the annual audit and tax clearance, but requires the bank to verify the distribution resolution, audited financial statements and tax withholding certificates; flexibility of currency conversion is at market rate but subject to anti-avoidance review. Surplus capital and loan principal repayments require SAFE registration and foreign debt quota limits. Overall, the regime is a managed float with daily reference rate fixing; the WFOE faces high compliance overhead for cross-border fund flows and must maintain a fully documented treasury file for each remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's Measures for Foreign Exchange Administration of Trade in Goods, export receipts from TIR trucking services and ancillary cargo charges are not subject to a fixed mandatory surrender ratio. A Chinese WFOE may retain foreign currency in its current-account FX account or sell on demand to designated banks. The statutory collection period is generally within 90 days after customs export declaration, with a permitted extension to 180 days for legitimate commercial delays. There is no compulsory conversion ratio to CNY; however, the receiving bank must perform genuine-transaction verification and report receipt amounts into SAFE's goods trade monitoring system. Receipts that remain outstanding beyond the prescribed timeframe without adjustment declaration will be flagged as overdue verification and may trigger regulatory review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI injection; Basic Operational Currency Account for daily CNY operations

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account plus Current Account Foreign Exchange Receipts Account
Basic Operational Currency Account for TIR fuel card settlement and payroll disbursements
Basic Operational Currency Account with integrated SWIFT and trade finance clearing facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited and conditional: a pure offshore EMI is not authorized by PBOC or SAFE to open local RMB or foreign exchange settlement accounts for a Chinese WFOE, and therefore cannot serve as the primary banking rail. A PBOC-licensed non-bank cross-border payment institution may be engaged only as an ancillary front-end for small ticket receipts or low-value disbursements, and all such flows must clear through a licensed domestic commercial bank for SAFE reporting, trade verification and capital account control. The WFOE should not outsource statutory FX compliance, TIR trade documentation or FDI capital supervision to any offshore EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a China WFOE, the registered statutory legal representative and the identified beneficial owner generally must appear in person at the initial account opening interview in a physical domestic branch. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as a substitute for the first identity verification under full-scope AML/KYC enhancement; however, after the face-to-face interview has been completed, subsequent operational signatories may be appointed through a notarized power of attorney that is consular legalized or apostilled where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A Taiwan-incorporated parent with nominee directors or incomplete beneficial ownership chain triggers enhanced ownership review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles of association and company registration from Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs, board minutes appointing the WFOE legal representative, audited parent financial statements, notarized beneficial ownership declaration, passport or national ID copies of all individuals above the equity threshold, bank reference from the parent's principal bank, and complete SAMR share transfer records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: WFOE registered address appears to be a virtual office or low-occupancy site, raising lack of operational substance concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current business license reflecting actual premise, valid lease or property ownership certificate, utility bills and site photography, payroll and social security filings proving local employees, vehicle fleet registration lists, and TIR carnet holder certificates proving active bonded trucking operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border TIR trucking raises trade-based money laundering risks through cargo misdeclaration and multi-country bonded transit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: TIR carnet holder certificate issued by the authorized national guaranteeing association, historical customs transit declarations, CMR consignment notes for each journey, transport insurance policy, itemized HS codes and declared cargo values, counterparty KYB files for freight clients, and a transport route plan reviewed by the bank's trade finance compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: TIR route coverage or counterparties may intersect US, EU or UN sanctions-affected jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative hit results from OFAC, EU consolidated and UN sanctions screening, a sanctions-free corridor map, attestation by the freight compliance officer, cargo end-user certificates, dual-use goods screening declarations, and an internal sanctions screening log with audit trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection from the Taiwan parent into the Chinese WFOE requires completion of FDI registration with SAFE and the relevant commerce authority. The bank opens a SAFE-designated FDI capital account and the Taiwan shareholder remits equity in USD, EUR, TWD or other freely usable currency via SWIFT MT103 using the FDI direct investment equity contribution purpose code. The receiving bank verifies the remittance against the SAFE FDI information system, issues an inbound remittance certificate, and records the capital account position. The capital may be converted into CNY upon actual use according to the FDI settlement policy, and a licensed CPA capital verification report is filed with SAMR following the capital contribution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for fuel, customs fees, cross-border freight costs, TIR carnet charges, maintenance and operational expenses should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 with attached contract and invoice matching, Commercial Letters of Credit for large documented trade transactions, and Documentary Collections where deferred documentary control is required. Each outward payment must be reported to SAFE using the true trade in goods or services purpose code, with transport contracts, invoices, customs declarations, CMR consignment notes and, where applicable, a tax payment certificate for service payments exceeding the tax authority threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards backed by genuine trade and transport-related exposure
FX swaps for short-term liquidity rebalancing between CNY and USD or CNY and EUR
Cross-currency swaps for approved foreign debt and loan principal hedging, not for speculative conversion of equity capital
FX options on a premium-paying hedging strategy only, with no net speculative position

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible as onshore WFOE hedging instruments under SAFE real-need principles; any NDF overlay must reside with the offshore ultimate parent and cannot be booked on the Chinese entity's treasury ledger

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting and adoption of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' Meeting of the WFOE; minutes and adopted statements maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end; for a calendar-year company no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties may be imposed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs on the responsible director; if the meeting is repeatedly not convened, the MOEA may order compulsory dissolution and an administrative strike-off of the company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return and financial statement tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May through 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; special fiscal-year companies file within five months after the fiscal year closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 1% monthly surcharge on underpaid tax capped at 12%; outstanding tax accrues postal-bank statutory interest; failure to file after demand may result in a penalty up to three times the underpaid tax, enforced asset collection, and eventual administrative dissolution for prolonged suspension of business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual company information confirmation and beneficial ownership/shareholder register reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual no-change confirmation on or before 30 June; any share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed within 15 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the shareholder information and UBO register filing obligations may expose the company and responsible officers to administrative fines and, for intentional false statements, criminal liability under the Money Laundering Control Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Registration verification and registered status maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs and local business registration office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the anniversary of the original company registration certificate; immediate update within 15 days of any change in directors, registered address, scope of business, or capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate registration may trigger penalty filings, cancellation of business recognition, and a regulatory bar on obtaining or renewing the road freight operating license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual road freight operating permit and TIR Carnet carrier authorization renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Highway Bureau, Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan, and Customs Administration for TIR authorization
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the MOTC operating permit; renewal application must be submitted at least 30 days before license expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operation without a renewed permit is an immediate violation of the Highway Act; penalties include per-vehicle fines, vehicle impoundment, suspension or revocation of the freight transport license, and automatic loss of TIR Carnet standing authorization.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20 and related MOEA enforcement rules, mandatory audit and certification by an independent licensed CPA is triggered if any one of the following is exceeded: paid-in capital above NT$50,000,000; annual operating revenue above NT$100,000,000; average workforce above 200 employees; outstanding bank credit at fiscal year-end above NT$30,000,000; or where the foreign-investment approval authority, tax administration, or financing banks require audited statements for the WFOE.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS (TIFRS) for companies meeting audit thresholds or otherwise required by the Financial Supervisory Commission; private WFOEs below the thresholds may apply the Taiwan SME Enterprise Accounting Standard under the Business Entity Accounting Act. Licensed cross-border trucking operations must also comply with MOTC-prescribed cost and revenue reporting formats.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must maintain a current register of shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners at its registered office. Annual confirmation of the UBO register is performed by the responsible director before the annual ordinary general meeting and evidenced in the minutes. Any share transfer, change in controlling shareholder, or material UBO change must be reported to the MOEA Company Registration System within 15 days, and the internal UBO register must be updated within 30 days of the transaction; false or absent UBO reporting triggers AML penalties and criminal liability.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan's Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Act provides a 20% headline rate. A 5% retained earnings surtax applies to undistributed net profits. Incentives include a 15% corporate income tax rate for qualified logistics and cross-border trading enterprises located in designated Free Trade Zones under the Act for Establishment and Management of Free Trade Zones; a 10% R&D investment tax credit under the Industrial Innovation Act; and a 10-year loss carryforward for enterprises maintaining proper books and filing on time.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 7501 – Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return; filed through the Ministry of Finance Electronic Tax Filing and Collection System (e-Filing portal) using the taxpayer's Unified Business Number (UBN).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with a provisional return due in September and monthly/quarterly instalments for large taxpayers).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual settlement return must be filed between 1 May and 31 May of the year following the fiscal year; the provisional return is due from 1 September to 30 September of the current year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Identification and Non-Resident Ownership Data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, Uniform Business Number (UBN), registered address, principal industry code (ISIC 5221 / NAICS 484121), date of incorporation, and identity of each shareholder or beneficial owner holding 10% or more.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the mainland Chinese shareholder's name, tax domicile, and ownership percentage. Attach the certificate of incorporation and, if treaty relief is claimed on future distributions, a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Chinese tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Accounting Period and Return Type
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year designation and whether the return is an annual settlement, short-period liquidation, insolvency proceeding, or branch-office return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE is a Taiwan resident entity, file on the worldwide income basis, with foreign tax credits for foreign-source income. If the Taiwan operation is a branch of the Chinese parent, report only Taiwan-source income and expenses attributable to the branch; branch profit remittances are subject to separate 20% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Gross Service Revenue (Cross-Border TIR Trucking)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue from cross-border bonded highway freight, including freight revenue for China–Taiwan legs, TIR carnet processing fees, fuel surcharge rebates, and logistics subcontracted revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue from transportation performed in Taiwan and from international carriage connected with Taiwan is Taiwan-source income. If revenue is shared with the foreign parent under a contractual arrangement, demonstrate the arm's-length split; a one-sided booking of revenue in a low-tax jurisdiction triggers a Box 3 adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Cost of Goods Sold / Direct Operating Costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs traceable to trucking services: diesel and fuel, road tolls, TIR carnet customs bonds, driver salaries and benefits, truck lease or depreciation, repairs, tyres, and insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibles must be supported by receipts or e-invoices. Payments to the Chinese parent for headquarters support, fuel procurement, or vehicle leasing are related-party transactions and must comply with transfer pricing documentation and 20% withholding when characterised as royalties or service fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit computed as Box 3 less Box 4, before operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If gross margin is outside the interquartile arm's-length range, prepare a contemporaneous transfer pricing report. Do not adjust away from a gross loss without evidence; the tax authority may apply the TNMM or cost-plus method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General administrative expenses, director fees, legal and accounting, office rent, utilities, communications, and depreciation not allocated to cost of goods sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to the mainland parent are deductible only if actually incurred, non-duplicative, and supported by service agreements and detailed records. Report foreign invoice payments on the annual payments-to-non-residents schedule and withhold 20% where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains and losses, gains or losses on disposal of vehicles, and other non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident related lender is deductible only at arm's-length rates and is subject to 20% statutory WHT, or 10% under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement if the lender is the beneficial owner holding a TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Net Profit / Assessable Income before Losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted by tax reconciliation, before deduction of prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Taiwan resident company, report worldwide income. Foreign-source income may be taxable with a foreign tax credit; for a branch of the Chinese parent, report only Taiwan-effect income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of net business losses from prior years, limited to the 10-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is denied if books are not properly kept, the return is late, or a more-than-50% ownership change occurs without business purpose. Losses from a permanent establishment outside Taiwan are not deductible against Taiwan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 – Taxable Income / Minimum Tax Base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss deductions, exemptions, and discretionary adjustments, and the alternative minimum tax (AMT) base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check whether profit retention triggers the 5% retained earnings surtax; full distribution of current profits avoids the surtax. Non-resident shareholder-level WHT is not computed on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 – Tax Rate and Basic Tax Computed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 20% statutory rate to taxable income, plus AMT if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned enterprises do not receive a reduced rate. Treaty relief on dividends is claimed at the withholding stage, not on the CIT return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment tax credits, R&D credits, foreign tax credits, and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For income taxed in mainland China, claim a foreign tax credit only if the same income is duplicate-taxed and a TRC is provided. Maintain the foreign tax credit calculation form and evidence of Chinese tax payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13 – Final Net Tax Payable / Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable less credits and provisional payments; if negative, the excess becomes a refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile any withholding on Taiwan-source income of the company. Confirm there are no outstanding withholding obligations on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under Income Tax Act Article 108, failure to file by 31 May imposes a surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax if filed after the deadline, increasing to 20% if an investigation has opened; daily interest accrues under Article 49 of the Tax Collection Act. Failure to file the provisional September return triggers a penalty of 5% of the estimated tax. Willful evasion is a criminal violation under Tax Collection Act Article 41, punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a fine up to NT$6 million; directors may be subjected to travel restriction orders where overdue tax and penalties exceed NT$1 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% for dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder; 21% for dividends paid to a non-resident individual. The Taiwanese resident company also suffers a 5% retained earnings surtax on undistributed net profits if earnings are accumulated without distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Chinese tax authority certifying fiscal residence; (2) file the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Treaty Relief Application before or at the time of payment; (3) provide a beneficial ownership declaration and, where required, proof of 25% shareholding to access the 5% dividend rate or 10% dividend rate otherwise, and the 10% interest/royalty rate; (4) post security if demanded by the Taiwan tax authority; and (5) if treaty relief is rejected, pay full statutory WHT and then file an amended return and refund application within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on interest paid to a non-resident corporate lender is 20%; statutory WHT on royalties or specialised technical service fees is 20%. Under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, interest and royalties paid to a mainland Chinese beneficial owner are reduced to 10%, provided a TRC is supplied and the beneficial ownership test is met. Intercompany freight procurement or fuel rebate payments that are not at arm's length may be recharacterised as constructive dividends and subjected to the full statutory WHT plus penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$100 million in aggregate related-party transactions (approximately USD 3.3 million) triggers mandatory Local File preparation; a Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above NT$20 billion, or where the Taiwanese entity's related-party transactions exceed NT$100 million in high-risk categories. Even below the threshold, a contemporaneous transfer pricing policy for TIR trucking revenue sharing is best practice.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Taiwan does not operate offshore ESR, the substance-over-form doctrine under Income Tax Act Article 12-1 and Article 43-1, together with the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement's treaty-beneficiary testing, require the Taiwan WFOE to demonstrate real board management in Taiwan, active contracts, local employees, truck ownership or qualifying leases, TIR carnet management, and actual Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Taiwan. The tax authority may ignore a shell WFOE and reattribute profits to the mainland parent; treaty relief is denied if the beneficial owner is merely a pass-through.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan WFOE exists only as a booking centre: no trucks, drivers, TIR carnet operations, or logistical management in Taiwan; board decisions are made in mainland China and invoices are issued through a Taiwanese shell without local substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority invokes Income Tax Act Article 12-1 (substance-over-form) and Article 43-1 (reallocation), disallowing expense deductions and assessing CIT at 20% on the reallocated net profit. An evasion penalty of 2 to 3 times the underpaid tax may be imposed under Article 110, and interest is added at the prescribed rate until payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the company's unpaid tax if the company is adjudged an artificial arrangement; civil actions permit asset seizure and restitution. Under Tax Collection Act Article 24, controlling directors can be blacklisted, given travel bans, and have personal bank accounts and properties attached for tax debts exceeding NT$1 million.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Evasion and False Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan entity makes intercompany payments to the mainland parent for management fees, technical royalties, and fuel procurement at inflated prices, stripping Taiwanese profit; no Local File documentation is maintained although related-party transactions exceed NT$100 million; e-invoices are fabricated to match the false cost allocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act Article 43-1, the tax authority reallocates profit and adds a penalty of 2 to 3 times the underpaid tax. Business Tax Act Article 51 also imposes a penalty of up to 5 times the sales tax evaded for false e-invoices, and the Ministry of Finance may suspend invoicing privileges or prohibit operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal charges under Tax Collection Act Article 41 (tax evasion by fraud): imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to NT$6 million. The corporate veil is pierced under Company Act Article 154 if the directors acted with bad faith, making them jointly and severally liable for all tax debts, compensation, and legal costs; a court may appoint a receiver to enforce against personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE distributes dividends to the mainland parent without withholding 20% WHT, mischaracterises the dividend as a repayment of shareholder loan or consulting fee, and obtains treaty relief based on a fraudulent Tax Residency Certificate from a shell Chinese entity that is not the true beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act Article 114, the company as withholding agent is liable for the full underwithheld tax plus a penalty equal to 20% of the underwithheld amount, or 40% for intentional failure; interest accrues from the date the tax should have been paid. Treaty abuse triggers reassessment at the statutory 20% rate, and the fraudulent TRC may be reported to tax authorities for criminal sanction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the withholding declaration or allowed payment without withholding are personally liable as withholding agents. Criminal liability under Tax Collection Act Article 42 can lead to imprisonment of up to 3 years for intentional withholding violations. Directors may also be disqualified as directors, banned from leaving Taiwan if the outstanding tax debt exceeds NT$1 million, and held personally liable for the corporation's tax debts where a court finds the distribution and fake documentation were a sham.
